newsitem.title: KUWAIT: KUWAIT-IRAN TO DISCUSS JOINT STEEL MILL PROJECT.
newsitem.headline: KUWAIT-IRAN TO DISCUSS JOINT STEEL MILL PROJECT.

text.p: Iranian Economy and Finance Minister Morteza Mohammadkhan said on Monday he will discuss with Kuwaiti officials a proposed joint steel mill project and expressed hope the two sides would agree to boost trade.

But he refused to say if the Gulf neighbours were close to finalising the $70 million project between the National Iranian Steel Company (Nisco) and private Kuwaiti investors to set up a steel reinforced bar mill in Kuwait.

"If we do not achieve the final conclusion of this project during the visit, talks will continue between us until we finalise this huge project," the minister, speaking through an Arabic translator, told reporters upon his arrival in Kuwait.
Mohammadkhan's team of about 17-members includes an official from the Mines and Metals Ministry.
The proposed mill is expected to produce about 300,000 tonnes a year while Kuwait's annual consumption is estimated at 400,000 tonnes. The production will be consumed domestically.
"We have had good and solid negotiations (on the project) and we will continue them during this visit," said Mohammadkhan, the third Iranian cabinet minister to visit Kuwait this year.
Nisco will have a 49 percent stake in the mill while Kuwaiti investors would hold the rest. The two states have also had preliminary talks on jointly building two cement plants in Kuwait.
"I hope this visit will lead to the aspired agreements. I hope it will be crowned at a high level to boost our trade and economic links," added Mohammadkhan.

His Kuwaiti counterpart Nasser al-Rodhan said the two states could conclude during the three-day visit "legal accords" to boost ties including agreements to avoid double taxation and the protection of investments.
The Iranian minister said the talks would centre on trade issues and boosting cooperation in fields of "technical and engineering services".
Kuwait Shipbuilding and Repairyard Co is due to complete "in the next few days" work on the first of four Iranian ports authority dredgers, an industry executive said.
Another two dredgers are due in Kuwait next month for repairs at the yard, which recently completed a life extension project on an Iranian bulk carrier, the source told Reuters.
Kuwait's ties with Iran improved after the Islamic republic took a neutral stand in the 1991 U.S.-led Gulf War to free Kuwait from a seven-month Iraqi occupation.
The trade balance is in favour of Kuwait which exports to non-Arab Iran refined oil products worth some $200 million a year while Iranian exports to Kuwait are worth about $85 million.
